title: Top Products by Revenue
description:
Merchandising wants a short leaderboard: the top products by discounted revenue for the overnight drop — not the full product rollup.

Read the input Parquet, compute per-`product_id` discounted revenue (same line formula as Aggregate Product Totals), assign a dense rank by revenue descending, keep rows with `rank <= 10`, and write Parquet with overwrite. Ties share a rank; because of dense ranking at the cutoff you may emit **more than 10 rows**.

Line revenue: `quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct)`, round half-up to 2 decimals per line, then sum. Order ranks by `total_revenue` desc, then `product_id` asc. Output columns only: `product_id`, `total_revenue` (DECIMAL(12,2)), `rank` (INT).

Input columns: `txn_id`, `product_id`, `store_id`, `quantity`, `unit_price`, `discount_pct`. Implement with Spark DataFrame APIs (`groupBy` / `agg`, window `dense_rank`) — no Python sorts over collected rows. **Run** uses two smoke testcases; **Submit** uses the full set and row-diffs your Parquet against each case’s `expected/`.

Write results with `df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(OUTPUT_PATH)`. `OUTPUT_PATH` is set by the platform for **this Run/Submit only**.

problemStatement.overview: Aggregate discounted revenue per product_id, dense-rank descending, keep rank <= 10, write Parquet to OUTPUT_PATH.
symptoms: Merchandising still scans the full product rollup to find overnight winners.
Ties at the cutoff must share a dense rank (may yield more than 10 rows).
yourTaskSteps: Read input Parquet from INPUT_PATH (platform stages selected testcase inputs).
Sum per-line discounted revenue (round half-up to 2 dp) by product_id.
dense_rank by total_revenue desc, product_id asc; keep rank <= 10.
Write product_id, total_revenue, rank to OUTPUT_PATH with overwrite.
problemStatement.yourTask: Implement src/main.py that emits the top products by revenue with dense rank.
hints: Reuse the Aggregate Product Totals line_revenue formula, then groupBy product_id.
Filter rank <= 10 after ranking — do not use a blind limit(10) if you need correct ties.
spark.read.parquet(INPUT_PATH) reads every staged testcase file.

Sum of per-line rounded discounted revenue (DECIMAL(12,2))
dense_rank: 1 = highest revenue; ties share a rank
